title: Kalidasa's Shakuntala (Abhijnanashakuntala)
summary: Shakuntala, the best-known work of the Sanskrit poet and dramatist Kalidasa, dramatises the epic tale of King Dushyanta, who forgets his secret marriage to Shakuntala until a lost ring is found. Scholars place Kalidasa in the Gupta period, probably the late 4th to early 5th century CE, with an association to Ujjain.

uncertainty.note: Encyclopedia.com gives active late 4th-early 5th century (and links the poet to Chandragupta II, 375-415); the Liberty Fund piece says there are no agreed dates and that most scholars place him in the Gupta dynasty. Aihole inscriptions show the works predate 634. A play-specific date is not given by either source.

as_recorded.value: There are no agreed upon dates for his life or even where he lived

where.modern_name: Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, India (proxy pin: sources associate the poet with Ujjain; the play's place of composition is not stated)
where.historical_name: Ujjayini (Ujjain), North India under the Gupta dynasty (association only)

importance.justification: Described by Encyclopedia.com as the best-known work of the poet who set the standard for classical Indian poetry and drama.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the date and place: both are for the poet, not for this play specifically, and sources conflict (other pages opened gave third to sixth centuries and wider). The Ujjain pin is a proxy for the poet's association.
